About IIC:
The Institution's Innovation Council (IIC) is an initiative of the Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India, established through the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell (MIC) in collaboration with the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE). The programme was launched in 2018 with the objective of systematically promoting innovation, entrepreneurship, and startup culture across Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) in India. The primary vision of IIC is to transform educational institutions into centres of innovation by encouraging students and faculty members to develop creative solutions to real-world problems through technology, research, and entrepreneurship. 

Every participating institution constitutes an Institution's Innovation Council comprising the Head of the Institution, faculty coordinators, innovation ambassadors, startup coordinators, incubation representatives, intellectual property rights (IPR) coordinators, industry experts, alumni entrepreneurs, and student representatives. This council plans and executes various innovation and entrepreneurship activities throughout the academic year based on the activity calendar provided by MoE's Innovation Cell. These activities include expert lectures, workshops, innovation competitions, hackathons, ideation sessions, startup boot camps, design thinking workshops, prototype exhibitions, patent awareness programmes, entrepreneurship development programmes, and interactions with successful entrepreneurs and investors. 

The major objectives of IIC are to create a vibrant innovation ecosystem within institutions, establish mechanisms to support startups, encourage students to identify societal problems and develop innovative solutions, facilitate pre-incubation and incubation support, promote intellectual property creation, and strengthen industry–academia collaboration. IIC also motivates institutions to formulate Innovation and Startup Policies, establish incubation centres, encourage multidisciplinary project development, and participate in national innovation initiatives such as Smart India Hackathon, Toycathon, Kavach, and other innovation challenges. 

A unique feature of the IIC programme is its structured performance evaluation system. Institutions conduct activities through an online portal where every programme is documented and assessed. Based on their annual performance, institutions receive star ratings and recognition from MoE's Innovation Cell. The evaluation considers factors such as the number and quality of innovation activities conducted, student participation, startup creation, patent filings, incubation support, industry collaboration, and overall contribution to innovation and entrepreneurship. This motivates institutions to continuously improve their innovation ecosystem. 

IIC plays a significant role in implementing the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which emphasizes experiential learning, multidisciplinary education, innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship. Through its nationwide network of thousands of institutions, IIC has successfully created awareness among students and faculty about startup culture, design thinking, intellectual property rights, product development, and commercialization of research outcomes. Today, it serves as one of India's largest innovation networks connecting academic institutions, industries, incubation centres, investors, startups, and government agencies to build an innovation-driven economy. By nurturing innovative thinking among young minds, IIC contributes significantly to India's vision of becoming a global leader in research, innovation, and entrepreneurship. 

Official Website: https://mic.gov.in/

IIC Portal: https://iic.mic.gov.in/
Yukthi:
YUKTI (Young India Ke Transforming Ideas)

YUKTI (Young India Ke Transforming Ideas) is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India, implemented through the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell (MIC) in collaboration with AICTE. YUKTI serves as the National Innovation Repository (NIR) that systematically identifies, documents, nurtures, and supports innovative ideas, prototypes, technologies, and startups emerging from Higher Education Institutions across the country. Its primary objective is to bridge the gap between innovative ideas generated in academic institutions and their successful transformation into commercially viable products, technologies, or startup ventures. 

The YUKTI platform enables students, faculty members, researchers, innovators, and startup teams to upload details of their ideas, proof-of-concept models, prototypes, innovations, business models, and startup initiatives through their respective institutions. These submissions are verified by the Institution's Innovation Council (IIC) before being recommended to the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell for inclusion in the National Innovation Repository. The repository acts as a centralized database of innovations developed across Indian academic institutions and provides visibility to promising technologies and entrepreneurial ventures. 

One of the major strengths of YUKTI is its comprehensive support ecosystem. Selected innovations receive expert mentoring from domain specialists, technical guidance for product development, intellectual property support for patent filing, assistance in business model development, incubation opportunities, funding guidance, and connections with angel investors, venture capitalists, industries, and startup incubators. This structured support enables innovators to convert academic research into market-ready products and sustainable business enterprises. 

YUKTI also encourages institutions to maintain institutional innovation repositories and continuously identify innovative projects developed by students and faculty members. The platform supports innovations at multiple stages, including idea generation, proof of concept, prototype development, technology validation, startup formation, and commercialization. Through continuous monitoring and mentorship, YUKTI ensures that innovative projects receive the necessary technical, financial, and entrepreneurial support required for successful implementation. Institutions can also nominate their best innovations for participation in various national innovation and startup programmes organized by the Ministry of Education and allied organizations. 

The initiative aligns closely with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, Startup India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, and the national vision of promoting innovation-led economic growth. By creating a nationwide repository of innovations and facilitating collaboration among academic institutions, industries, investors, incubators, and government agencies, YUKTI strengthens India's innovation ecosystem. It encourages problem-solving, design thinking, interdisciplinary research, technology commercialization, and entrepreneurship among students and researchers.

Today, YUKTI has become an important platform for identifying grassroots innovations and providing innovators with opportunities to showcase their work at national forums, secure funding, obtain mentorship, and build successful startups. It plays a significant role in transforming academic ideas into impactful products and services that address societal challenges while contributing to India's knowledge economy and startup ecosystem. 

Official Website: https://mic.gov.in/ 

YUKTI Innovation Repository: https://yukti.mic.gov.in/
